subject: MedCore — evaluation onramp: Redwood-run benchmark checklist and scoring guide
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@medcorehealth.com>, Alex Park <alex.park@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + Redwood-run eval checklist (next steps)

Hi Emma / Alex —

Thanks again for the product demo this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned for a Redwood-run evaluation tailored to your triage summarization workflow: 

Key constraints we heard
- Short clinical notes (avg 120 tokens), need sub-1s per-call latency for summary generation
- Sensitive PHI; MedCore will run in a Private deployment (VPC)
- Baseline: current in-house model scores 0.78 F1 on the existing QA set

Proposed Redwood-run eval items (we can run these on your behalf):
1) Model candidate sweep: llama-3-70B-instruct-quant and redwood-optimized-13B-qlora (we will include a smaller llm for latency baseline).
2) Dataset format: CSV with columns [id, prompt, reference_summary, metadata_json]. See attached medcore_sample_prompts.csv for example rows.
3) Scoring: ROUGE-L and a clinical fact-check pass (binary per-reference) + custom severity-weighted F1. We’ll produce the scoring script and baseline_scoring_template.xlsx.
4) Prompt sets: we'll propose 3 prompt variants (concise, structured bullet, and extraction-first) to assess quality/regression risk.

Immediate next steps I suggest:
- You drop the first 500 annotated examples into the Drive folder (see link) OR share S3 read-only with our ingestion account.
- We send the Redwood-run eval config and scoring template by EOD Monday.
- Schedule a 30-min kickoff for ingestion and permission checks (I propose Tue 7/21 10am PT).

Attachments: medcore_sample_prompts.csv (sample rows), redwood_medcore_eval_instructions.pdf (eval runbook).

Thanks — happy to tweak based on your security / compliance checklist.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference, Inc.
D: +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + Redwood-run eval checklist (next steps)

Diego — good recap. Couple of internal notes before we finalize the config: 

- For the clinical fact-check pass, let's include a lightweight PII-sanitize step prior to scoring to avoid exposing PHI to external annotators. We should document that in the runbook.
- For latency baselines, include: 1) cold-start token path and 2) warmed KV-cache path for the 13B quant variant. That will show realistic user experience once caching is primed.
- I can prep the initial scoring script (python) and attach the baseline_scoring_template.xlsx in the drive. Marissa, can you own the prompt variants and create the first prompt_set_v1?

-Karthik

On Sun, Jul 19, 2026 at 08:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Will do — I'll throw together prompts for concise vs structured. Also propose a small holdout for safety/regression checks (50 items).
> 
> Marissa
From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@medcorehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@medcorehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + Redwood-run eval checklist (next steps)

Diego — thanks for the clear plan. A few questions from our side before we drop data: 

1) Is the sample CSV safe to upload as-is (contains de-identified notes)? We will be able to provide de-identified examples but need to confirm the minimal fields you need.
2) Who on Redwood will have access to the raw text during the Redwood-run? We prefer that only named engineers involved in the run have read permissions and that all access is logged.
3) For the clinical fact-check binary, can you share an example rubric?

We put the 500-row sample in the Drive folder this morning (link included). Happy to join Tue 10am PT for the kickoff.

—Emma
Principal Product Manager | MedCore Health
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@medcorehealth.com>, Alex Park <alex.park@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + Redwood-run eval checklist (next steps)

Emma — great, appreciate the upload. Quick answers and meeting invite sent: 

1) Sample CSV: yes — de-identified is perfect. Minimum columns we need: id, prompt, reference_summary, source_note_type. The medcore_sample_prompts.csv has example formatting; if you need a privacy checklist we can provide a one-pager.
2) Access: Redwood engineer access will be scoped to a named list. For this run: Karthik Iyer (inference lead), Marissa Cole (ops lead), and one backend engineer (will be listed in the kickoff). All access will be via your Private deployment (no data leaves MedCore VPC) and we will provide an access log for the ingestion window. Noting your logging requirement for the record.
3) Fact-check rubric: attached baseline_scoring_template.xlsx includes a draft binary rubric and severity weights. We'll iterate after the kickoff.

Next: I've scheduled the 30-min ingestion kickoff for Tue 2026-07-21 10:00 PT and shared calendar invites. See Drive and HubSpot links above.

Looking forward — we’ll run the Redwood evaluation and return a report with model recommendations, latency/cost tradeoffs, and the regression-risk heatmap.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: baseline_scoring_template.xlsx
